title: Home Purchase Financing Contract — Late Charge Clause and Grace Period
content:
**Late charge clause (Home Purchase Financing retail installment contract)**

(a) **When a charge may be assessed.** A late charge may be assessed only after the grace period has ended, counted from the installment due date. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the due date, so the charge may be assessed no earlier than the day after the due date plus the program's grace days. The due date used is the due date of the oldest unpaid installment as the company's loan record shows it.

(b) **Amount — retired clause.** *"The charge is the program's late-charge percentage of the monthly principal-and-interest amount, raised to the program's late-charge floor and capped at the program's late-charge cap, rounded half up to the cent." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis and is kept here only as a record.*

(c) **One per installment.** At most one late charge is assessed per installment.

(d) **Installments not charged.** No late charge is assessed on an installment that was paid in full within the grace period and is short only because an earlier late charge or fee is unpaid, and none on an installment moved by a deferment agreement.

### Grace period boundary (hypothetical dates, a grace period taken as 15 days)

| Due date | Grace days run | Assessment date | May the charge be assessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-03-01 | 2026-03-02 through 2026-03-16 | 2026-03-16 | no — the grace period has not ended |
| 2026-03-01 | 2026-03-02 through 2026-03-16 | 2026-03-17 | yes — the day after the due date plus 15 days |

The boundary is exclusive of the grace period itself: on the last grace day no charge may be assessed; on the following day it may.

superseded_clauses: The charge is late_charge_pct_of_installment percent of the monthly principal-and-interest amount, raised to late_charge_min and capped at late_charge_max for the program, rounded half up to the cent.
